title: How a counter wraps
modelNote: Each tick adds one. This teaching counter keeps only {width} bits; the lesson program uses {realWidth}-bit registers. Its readings are unsigned: zero or positive.
instruction: Press +1 to add a tick. Keep pressing until the stored reading returns to zero. Watch Carry out at the wrap. Reset starts at zero.
initialNote: The dash means no addition is shown yet.
forwardWrapped: The extra carry lies beyond the {width} stored bits. The stored bits wrap to zero.
backwardWrapped: Subtraction must borrow one group of {range} from the next position. Taking one leaves {stored} in {width} bits.
forwardNormal: The addition stays within the stored bits. Carry out is zero.
backwardNormal: The subtraction stays at or above zero. No borrow from beyond the stored bits is needed.
architectureNote: The carry shown belongs to this four-bit model. RISC-V has no carry flag.
initialStatus: Stored reading: {stored}. No step is shown.
borrowTitle: Optional: subtract one and inspect the borrow
borrowIntro: The processor’s arithmetic and logic unit (ALU) can subtract when an instruction such as sub requests it. Subtracting one is a decrement. This separate {width}-bit counter explores subtraction; it does not reverse time or undo an earlier operation.
borrowInstruction: Press −1 once from zero. Inspect Borrow needed and the stored reading. Keep pressing to count down through further wraps. Reset starts this counter at zero.
borrowInitialNote: The dash means no subtraction is shown yet.
borrowArchitectureNote: This marker describes borrow beyond the four stored bits. RISC-V has no borrow flag.
